To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

proNGF induces growth cone retraction in cultured hippocamp al neurons by binding to a complex of p75 NTR and SorCS2, resulting in dissociation of the Trio guan ine nucleotide ex change factor from the p75 NTR-SorCS 2 complex, and inactivation of Rac, which leads to growth cone collapse and retraction.
the proNGF-p75NTR-Sortilin complex induces neurite retraction by initiating two distinct signaling mechanisms.

proNGF, but not mature NGF, triggers acute growth cone collapse by binding to p75NTR/SorCS2, thereby inducing the dissociation of Trio, resulting in decreased activation of the GTPase Rac and the inactivation of fascin, leading to the collapse of actin-rich growth cone protrusions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate neuronal growth cone dynamics and the role of the p75 receptor family in these processes.
the molecular mechanisms of axon guidance, neuronal survival, and neurite outgrowth.
the role of neurotrophin receptors in the control of neurite outgrowth and retraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proNGF is a bifunctional molecule that can either promote or repress neuronal morphogenesis depending on the developmental stage and the cellular context in which it is expressed.
pro-NGF induces growth cone collapse and retraction in cultured hippocampcal neurons through two independent mechanisms, one involving Rac and the other involving fascin.
pro-NGF is an important regulator of neuronal morphological plasticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p75 receptor is a receptor that can signal both pro- and anti-survival signals.
proNGF promotes growth cone collapse and neurite retraction in hippocampal neurons through a p75NTR/SorCS2-dependent mechanism.

proNGF induces growth cone collapse through two distinct pathways: (i) by dissociating the guanine nucleotides exchange factor Trio from p75NTR/SorCS2, which results in the inactivation of the Rac GTPase; and (ii) by stimulating the inactivation of fascin, an actin bundling protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p75 neuro-trophin receptor (NTR) and SorCS-2 are involved in growth cone collapse and that this is mediated by Rac and fascin.
proNGF is a potent retraction factor for growth cones and dendrites of cultured hippocampi.
there is a bifunctional nature of p75NTR, and this is important for the development and maintenance of the nervous system.
